title: Waiver registry — /waivers/{node_id}.json and /waivers/all.json
description:
The published waiver registry: one document per repository, plus a global `/waivers/all.json` whose entries each carry `repoNodeId`. The second of the three inputs to the coverage function (`cov-v1`; FS-10 §4.2); it reads none for a repository with no published record, since a waiver is published under a record's node id. Waivers are gratis and are granted only by a claimed admin from the platform dashboard (D14) — they can never enter the registry by pull request, which is why the P-M2 registry source has no waivers field at all (FS02-060). At P-M2 every document is the honest empty state `waivers: []`, and the project page says so in words rather than showing a zero (VS-18). `coolingEndsAt` (= grantedAt + 72 h, D14 as amended) is consumed by VESTING only (FS05-063): a waiver inside its cooling window is coverage-eligible exactly like any other, because cooling governs whether vesting attaches permanently, never today's coverage answer. Revocation is PROSPECTIVE: `revokedAt` in the past removes coverage from that instant onward while the certificate verify record still attests the historical window (CERT-042).

A waiver covers from the instant it is RECORDED, not from the administrator's click (D68 item 8): its public entry and the log evidence for it (its certificate's `issue` entry in the transparency log) are published, and the registry then appends a `record` entry to the log (`ct-segment.v1` 1.4.0). That entry's `ts` is the waiver's `grantedAt`, and its 72 hours count from it. The decision instant is never published, and a click that never publishes covers nobody. A waiver whose evidence is public and which is not yet recorded is listed in `recording[]`, never in `waivers[]`, and covers nobody: the coverage function reads `waivers[]` alone. Every instant a waiver carries is whole UTC seconds, spelled `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, so a reader with a millisecond clock and one with a finer clock give the same answer at every boundary.

x-psn.phase: P-M2 (honest empty state) · populated at P-M3

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. `platform` is the P-M3 producer of record — the platform database, rendered by `jobs.index-build`. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`. The enum widens additively when the P-M3 producer takes a value of its own, and `platform` (2026-09-12) is that widening: `jobs.index-build` writes it in `PSN_ENV=prod` and writes `fixture` in every other environment, so a reader can still tell a production plane from a synthetic one by the label alone.

nodeId.description: Present on a per-repository document; absent on the global `/waivers/all.json`, whose entries carry `repoNodeId` instead.

scope.description: Which document this is. `repo` ⇒ `nodeId` is set; `all` ⇒ every entry sets `repoNodeId`.

waivers.description: Waiver grants. An empty array is a valid and expected state — it means no waiver exists, not that data is missing.

recording.description: Waivers being recorded: the waiver's certificate has its `issue` entry in the transparency log, and the registry has not yet appended the `record` entry that starts its coverage (D68 item 8). An entry here covers NOBODY, has no `grantedAt` and no `coolingEndsAt`, and is never read by the coverage function or the vesting generator. Once recorded, the waiver leaves this array and enters `waivers[]` with `grantedAt` = the `record` entry's `ts`. A waiver withdrawn before it was recorded stays here with `withdrawnAt`, as "withdrawn, never in force" (D71 item 2), and never enters `waivers[]`. A waiver with no log evidence is published nowhere. Emitted only when non-empty: absent means no waiver is being recorded, so a document with none keeps the bytes it had before this member existed.

repoNodeId.description: Required in `/waivers/all.json`; redundant (and normally omitted) in a per-repository document.

grantedAt.description: The instant the waiver was recorded: its entry and its log evidence published (D68 item 8). Coverage starts here, cooling window notwithstanding. On an entry with `record.recordSeq` it equals the `ts` of that `record` entry in the transparency log. An entry without `record.recordSeq` was published before recording existed (a development plane's test grants only; a production plane has none) and carries the grant's own instant, floored to the second. Whole UTC seconds.

coolingEndsAt.description: grantedAt + 72 h (D14 as amended). Vesting-only input (FS05-063); cov-v1 ignores it. Whole UTC seconds.

revokedAt.description: Prospective revocation instant: the `ts` of the waiver certificate's `revoke` entry in the transparency log (D71 item 1). An entry without `record.recordSeq` (published before recording existed, as for `grantedAt`) carries the grant's own revocation instant, floored to the second. Absent or null ⇒ live. A waiver gives permission from `grantedAt` and vests nothing before `coolingEndsAt`; one revoked INSIDE the cooling window vests nothing at all. Revocation never makes use permitted before it unlawful (Licence 1.0 §9). Whole UTC seconds.

grantedBy.description: Only a claimed repository admin can grant a waiver (D14). Recorded so the artifact carries its own provenance; no other value is issuable.

note.description: Optional public note from the granting admin. Repository-side content — escaped on render.

record.description: Where the waiver stands in the transparency log, by ids and sequence numbers only. With `recordSeq`, the entry at `recordSeq` is of kind `record`, its `ref` is the `h` of the `issue` entry at `issueSeq`, and its `ts` equals `grantedAt`; a reader holding the log checks all three. Absent on an entry published before recording existed.

reviews.description: The waiver's `under-review` annotation (FS12-018; FS-12 §9.8 step 3; G7.8, G10.4; FS-00 §6.2's dated note of 2026-10-26). A steward opens a review on a waiver granted in the exposure window of an administrator-account takeover, or classed as probable compromise, ONLY once the waiver is past its cooling window (`coolingEndsAt`); a waiver still inside it is voided instead (FS12-019). Append-only and oldest first: each item is one review, `since` the instant it began. At most one item is open (it has no `endedAt`), and only the last item can be open. A forward record closes the open item by writing its `endedAt`; no item is ever removed or rewritten, and a later review appends a new item (annotation, never deletion, SEC-07). The annotation carries no free text, no reason and no actor. Absent until a steward opens the first review, so an entry never reviewed keeps the bytes it had. `cov-v1` and the vesting generator IGNORE it: a waiver under review covers and vests exactly as it would without it, and coverage changes only through `revokedAt`.

review.description: One review of a waiver: when it began and, once a forward record closed it, when it ended. Nothing else.

since.description: The instant the steward opened the review. Never earlier than the waiver's `coolingEndsAt`, and never earlier than the previous item's `endedAt`. Whole UTC seconds.

endedAt.description: The instant the forward record closed the review; never earlier than `since`. Absent while the review is open. Whole UTC seconds.

recordingEntry.description: One waiver being recorded, or withdrawn before it was ever recorded. It has no `grantedAt`, no `coolingEndsAt` and no `revokedAt`: it was never in force.

wvrId.description: Waiver ULID, lowercase Crockford, `wvr_` prefixed (FS-00 §6.1). The same id the entry keeps in `waivers[]` once recorded.

repoNodeId.description: Required in `/waivers/all.json`; redundant (and normally omitted) in a per-repository document.

beneficiary.description: Who the waiver will cover once recorded, published exactly as its `waivers[]` entry will publish it.

record.description: The waiver certificate and its `issue` entry in the transparency log: the evidence that is public. No `recordSeq`: nothing is recorded yet.

withdrawnAt.description: Present once the waiver was withdrawn before it was recorded: the `ts` of its certificate's `revoke` entry (D71 items 1 and 2). The entry then reads "withdrawn, never in force" and stays listed. Whole UTC seconds.

record.description: A waiver's place in the transparency log, by ids and sequence numbers only: no name, no subject, nothing the log itself does not already carry (D65; `ct-segment.v1`).

certId.description: The waiver's `license-status` certificate (variant `waiver`); its verify record is `/certs/{certId}.json`. The route by which the company proves coverage with its own credential: the SHA-256 of its JWS equals the `h` of the entry at `issueSeq`.

issueSeq.description: The global `seq` of that certificate's `issue` entry in the transparency log.

recordSeq.description: The global `seq` of the `record` entry that recorded the waiver. Its `ts` is the waiver's `grantedAt`. Present on every recorded waiver.

beneficiary.description: Who the waiver covers. Every grant mints an UNVERIFIED `co_` stub plus a registry entry at grant time, so a beneficiary with no account and no verified domain still resolves by ULID (FS-10 §4.3 step 2 — the reachability rule). Name-only lookups are answered by this public artifact, never by cov-v1, and only for a named beneficiary. One shape for a `waivers[]` entry and a `recording[]` entry. A named beneficiary (`display` `named`, or absent) carries `name`; a masked one (`display` `masked`) carries neither `name` nor `domain`.

display.description: Whether the public entry names the company (`named`) or masks it (`masked`) (D66 item 3). Public naming needs the company's documented agreement (D66 item 3). The repository's administrators choose per waiver at the grant, masked by default, and name the company, at the grant or by lifting a mask later, only with that agreement; a name once published is never masked again, except for a correction the law requires (D66 item 3; platform migration 0106). A masked company stays visible to the repository's administrators, its contributors, the company itself and the Association, and to nobody else, save a disclosure the law requires (D65 item 1, D66 items 1 and 2); the public entry still names the project, the scope, the dates and the status (D65 item 1). Absent reads as `named`: every entry published before this member existed names its company, and the producer writes `display` on every entry from the slice that honours it (ORC-37 W4). No masked waiver is published on production before the licence carries masking (licence §2 and §9; D65 item 5) and the other conditions of D65 item 5 hold.

coId.description: The company's id, which cov-v1 matches first. On a masked entry it is kept FOR NOW only, so that cov-v1 keeps matching a masked waiver on a development plane (the orchestrator's word of 2026-10-21 on L2.3-03). D65 item 5 bars the shared company id on a masked public entry, because `/entitlements/{coId}.jws` (the verified domains) and `covered-organisations` (the name, when listed) re-identify the company. So no masked waiver is published on production while its entry carries `coId`. A follow-up slice (PS-2205, after the coverage route from the company's own certificate, PS-1913) stops writing `coId` on a masked entry, and this description and the masked `cov-v1` vector change in place; from then on a masked waiver is covered only through the company's own certificate.

name.description: The company's name. Present on a named beneficiary, and only there.

domain.description: Matched by cov-v1 only against a company's VERIFIED domains. Never on a masked beneficiary.

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).
